exact_source.author: Chiara Meroni
exact_source.title: Directional Convexity (problems 34 and 35)
exact_source.locator: Open Problem 35 (Conditions for semialgebraic D-convex hulls)

method_outcomes.B1: Reframed the finite-support Jensen condition as dual membership against the evaluation-difference cone induced by all D-convex functions; this isolates the missing finite real-algebraic representation theorem but does not itself supply one.
method_outcomes.B17: Compared the hidden Jensen-weight object with biconvex martingales, laminate/Jensen measures, and finite planar D-convex algorithms. These give representation or projected membership machinery, but the bounded search found no theorem giving semialgebraicity of the full parametric weight relation.
method_outcomes.B27: Strengthened the target to Jensen-tameness: semialgebraicity of the full relation J_D(P) for every finite support. The prior minimal-fiber theorem makes this product-stable and natural, but equivalence with the source property for a fixed D remains unproved because projection can hide nonsemialgebraic fibers.

exact_blocker: Characterize all cones D subset R^d such that for every finite K subset R^d, the functional D-convex hull conv_D(K) is semialgebraic; after prior reductions, the operative gap is deciding when {x : Lambda_D(P,x) is nonempty} is semialgebraic for every finite P while Lambda_D is defined by all D-convex Jensen inequalities.
simplest_unproved_case: For three normalized planar directions D3 and arbitrary affinely spanning four-point planar support P, decide whether the full Jensen relation J_D3(P) is semialgebraic. The hidden barycentric fiber is one-dimensional.
nearest_solved_technique: Extend the finite planar Franek-Matousek functional D-convex hull machinery from projected membership to the full scalar Jensen-weight relation, using biconvex/martingale language only as a translation aid.
source_status: OPEN in the bounded 2026-09-17 source/literature check; no source-complete characterization located. Search miss is not a novelty certificate.
